v0.6.name: Crew
v0.6.features:
Agreed with the player (stages 1-3 done). Build ALL of these:

CARRY-OVERS
- Realistic deadhead airlines: prefer the low-cost carrier based at the origin/destination (Ryanair at STN/DUB/BGY..., easyJet at LGW/LTN/GVA..., Wizz at BUD/OTP..., Vueling at BCN, Transavia at ORY/AMS...), then airlines of the origin/destination country, then hub connections; never put an airline on a route it doesn't realistically fly (known bad picks: STN-DUB on Aer Lingus instead of Ryanair; LDE-LIS on easyJet; TFS->OTP via IST). Add tests over a sample of route pairs.
- Pacing tune: bot seed 2 gets only 1.4 meaningful actions/week (target >= 1/week on every seed incl. 1-6, ideally ~2) and governments pay late only 2/5 (target 'mostly late'). Tune offer/decision pacing and government late-payment odds without making the game easier.

1. ROSTER BOARD: a crew x day grid like a real crew-control screen: rows = crew (grouped by base/rank/type, filterable), columns = days (zoom week <-> month, scroll), cells show duties (flight numbers/route), days off, standby, sick, training/conversion, joining, positioning and deadheading, using the same colours/labels as the v0.5.2 crew calendar. Drag and drop a duty from one crew member to another to swap/reassign, with live FTL legality while dragging (green ok / red illegal with the reason) and the existing manual-assignment rules (locked assignments survive re-plans). iPad touch first (long-press to pick up, drag, drop), large targets, smooth scrolling with ~120 crew x 31 days.

2. BULK TYPE-RATING CONVERSION (replaces the bigger 'training & currency' idea; keep it simple): the player selects many crew at once (multi-select in the Crew list and on the roster board) and sends them on a type conversion to another aircraft type (e.g. A320 -> A330). The game groups them into classes automatically: pilots in pilot classes, cabin crew in cabin classes, max 20 per classroom (overflow makes additional classes, staggered if needed). Pilots take much longer (realistic: ~5-7 weeks incl. ground school, simulator and base/line training) than cabin crew (~1-2 weeks). Each class shows on every member's roster as a block labelled e.g. 'Conversion A330' (in the crew calendar strip, the roster board, and the Crew list status). Costs per head (pilots much more expensive) go through the ledger. While converting they can't fly; after completion they hold the new rating (decide and document whether they keep the old one — realistic for cabin crew to hold up to 3 types, pilots usually one type unless common type rating like A330/A350 or A320 family). Planning UI shows start/end dates, who's in which class, cost, and warns if it leaves the current fleet short of legal crew.

3. MORALE & ATTRITION: morale (already 0-100 on crew) is driven by tour length, days off, time away from base, hotel standard, per-diem policy, late-notice roster changes and mission type (evacuation/humanitarian lift morale; deportation/controversial flights lower it); company policies the player sets (hotel standard, per-diem level, max tour length) trade money for morale. Low morale raises sick calls, lowers service (affects client satisfaction/reputation slightly) and eventually crew resign with a notice period (shown on the roster and in the inbox) so the player must re-hire. Visible on crew cards, a company-wide morale indicator, and clear inbox messages. Balance: noticeable but not punishing when the player is reasonable.

4. EXTRA CREW ABOVE THE LEGAL MINIMUM: per aircraft (and optionally per contract) the player can set extra cabin crew above ceil(seats/50) (and an extra pilot where useful). Extra crew cost salary/per diem, improve crew morale (lighter workload) and service quality (client satisfaction, small reputation effect), and some clients (VIP, sports, long-haul) request or pay for it. The auto-roster honours it; legality and costs follow.

v0.7.name: Fleet & Ladder
v0.7.features:
Agreed with the player (stages 1-3 done). Build ALL of these:

CARRY-OVERS FROM v0.6 READINESS (fix first)
- Bulk conversion modal: when a red 'fleet short of legal crew' warning is shown, Book must ask for an explicit confirm (one tap must never ground the fleet).
- Roster board perf at 4×: memoise rows per crew/version or throttle refresh to ~1 Hz while the clock runs (p99 was 50 ms with 4× CPU throttle).
- Deadhead carriers still unrealistic in places: DXB–LIS on TAP (TAP doesn't serve DXB; Emirates does), LIS–SOF and HAM–BOJ via SOF on Bulgaria Air, LGW–GVA on Swiss (easyJet flies LGW–GVA). Add per-airline reach/avoid lists (hubs, bases, realistic networks) and a test table of ~40 route pairs with the expected carrier.
- Pacing: seed 2 has 41/52 active weeks (target ≥ 42); loosen the quiet-week floor slightly.
- Flaky timing test under load in board.test.ts/roster.test.ts: widen the budget or make it deterministic.

6. SCARCE AIRCRAFT MARKET: used aircraft for sale, dry-lease-in offers from real lessors, rare new-delivery slots, and lease returns at the end of leases (return conditions and costs). Offers are scarce and stay open for days; deliveries take weeks to months. A bought/leased aircraft is DELIVERED AT THE SELLER'S/LESSOR'S LOCATION (a real airport somewhere in the world), appears there on the map, and the game plans a FERRY flight to the player's base (pilots only, shown on the map as a ferry with its path, with fuel/crew costs and FTL; tech stops if range requires). The DELIVERY PILOTS first DEADHEAD on real commercial airline flights from their base (or wherever they are) to the aircraft's location, and those commercial flights are shown on the map exactly like the v0.5.2 crew deadheads (grey icon, floating flight-number label e.g. 'TP 1342', thin grey dotted path, tap for airline/flight no./route/times/time to landing/crew on board), with connections as separate legs; then they fly the delivery ferry home. Their rosters show the deadhead + ferry + rest. A Settings toggle turns ON/OFF a notification (inbox + quiet toast, optional auto-pause) whenever a new buying/leasing option appears on the market.

7. CABIN RECONFIGURATION: all-economy, two-class or VIP layouts per aircraft; a refit takes the aircraft out of service for days-weeks (at a capable MRO station) and costs money; the layout changes seats and decides which contracts it can bid for (VIP/sports want premium cabins, Hajj/troop rotations want max seats); feasibility explains it; shown on Fleet cards and the Schedule.

8. THE LADDER (approvals & bigger aircraft): an approvals tree — ETOPS 120 -> 180 -> 240, widebody operations, long-haul with augmented crews, ultra-long-haul (FRMS) — each needs time, money, trained/rated crew and a clean record; approvals gate which aircraft types and contracts are available, unlocking the 767/A330, then the 777, then the A350-ULR and prestige long-haul work. Clear progression UI (a tree/ladder on the Company screen with requirements and progress) and goals that celebrate each step.

v0.8.name: World
v0.8.features:
Agreed with the player (stages 1-3 done). Build ALL of these:

9. MORE CONTRACT TYPES: Hajj airlifts (big seasonal pilgrim flights; dates drift ~11 days earlier each year with the Islamic calendar; max-seat cabins), UN multi-year rotations, VIP & presidential (high pay, high standards, premium cabins, extra crew), deportation flights (well paid; hurt reputation and crew morale — a moral choice), war-zone evacuations (war-risk insurance cost, danger, urgency), medical/air-ambulance style charters, music tours (multi-city routing), Antarctica flights (special approvals/runways). Each with realistic pay, requirements, feasibility explanations and flavour text with real clients.

10. RIVAL OPERATORS WITH PERSONALITIES: real ACMI operators (Hi Fly, Wamos Air, euroAtlantic, Getjet, Airhub, Avion Express, Titan Airways, Privilege Style, Air Atlanta Icelandic, Heston, KlasJet, Smartwings, Global Crossing...) each with a style (aggressive pricing, prestige, reliability, size), fleets that change over time, competing bids so the player sometimes loses work to a cheaper/closer rival (with an explanation), and sub-chartering BOTH ways (hire a rival when stuck; rivals ask the player to fly for them). A rivals view on the Company screen.

11. MARKET CYCLES: fuel price moves (affects charters/ferries and some offers), seasonality (summer peak, winter trough, Hajj season), and demand shocks (an airline collapse creates ACMI demand; recession lowers it); visible as a simple market outlook and in offer volume/pricing.

12. INVENTED WORLD EVENTS: coups, strikes, volcanic ash, natural disasters, airline failures, wars, airspace closures, etc. in real places involving real airlines/governments (the player explicitly wants invented events — BRIEF 'Player decisions'); they create urgent work (evacuations, AOG/ACMI demand), risks (airspace closures reroute or cancel flights, insurance) and opportunities, announced in the inbox and on the map (e.g. a shaded closed airspace).

v0.9.name: Experience
v0.9.features:
Agreed with the player (stages 1-3 done). Build ALL of these:

5. UNLOCKABLE AUTOMATION (department heads earned through achievements; the player wants to struggle first and feel accomplishment): Ops Control duty manager (unlock: 25 sectors with no illegal duty) handles routine delays and sick call-ins with the player's default rules; Maintenance planner (unlock: first C-check completed on time) auto-books A-checks into maintenance nights; Crew scheduling desk (unlock: 2 months at >= 98% crew coverage) repairs the roster after disruptions and manages extra crew; Commercial analyst (unlock: 5 contracts completed) scores offers vs the fleet and suggests counter-prices; Credit control (unlock: first late government payment collected) chases late payers and sets terms; Fleet & positioning planner (unlock: first widebody) proposes ferry/positioning plans and tech stops; Custom alert & auto-pause rules (unlock: reputation 'Reliable'). Each is a hire with a monthly salary and a skill level that can make mistakes, can be overridden or switched off, and never takes the big decisions (which contracts, which aircraft, crises). Unlock moments are celebrated.

14. ACHIEVEMENTS, SOUND & TUTORIAL HINTS: achievements for milestones (with a gallery on the Company screen and calm unlock toasts); calm optional sound and ambient audio generated with WebAudio (no audio files needed unless tiny ones are justified): soft UI clicks, inbox chime, cockpit-style ding for decisions, faint airport/cabin ambience — all with a Settings master switch and volume, OFF by default if autoplay rules require; gentle first-time tutorial hints per screen (dismissible, 'don't show again', reset in Settings), written for an ACMI insider (no condescension).
